sources.title: Participating in the UK ETS
facts: Updated 1 July 2026.
Installations and aircraft operators submit verified emissions by 31 March and surrender allowances by 30 April; maritime entered the scheme from 1 July 2026.
Compliance obligations and permits or monitoring plans do not themselves create parcel-level measurements.

sources.title: UK ETS for aviation: how to comply
facts: Aviation scheme years run 1 January to 31 December.
Aviation CO2 is monitored under an emissions monitoring plan and reported by 31 March.
Verified operator emissions are not cadastral parcel emissions.

sources.title: CORSIA: how to comply
facts: CORSIA covers monitored CO2 from international flights for each scheme year.
Verified reports are due by 30 April and eligible emission units address offsetting obligations.
Offsets and reported flight emissions must not be promoted to land-parcel observations.

sources.title: UK ETS Aviation Allocation Table
facts: Last updated 13 April 2026.
The table records free-allocation entitlements for aircraft operators for the 2021 to 2025 allocation period.
Allowance entitlement is not a physical emissions measurement.

sources.title: UK ETS Allocation Table for operators of installations
facts: Last updated 17 April 2026.
The table covers installation free allocations for the 2021 to 2026 period and reflects activity-level changes.
Allocated allowances are not measured emissions.

sources.title: UK ETS Registry public reports
facts: 2026 installation and aircraft account-holder/allocation reports were published 5 July 2026.
The compliance report contains emissions and surrendered allowances for scheme years 2021 to 2025.
Registry compliance and transaction records require scope and account interpretation and do not imply parcel binding.

sources.title: HSE emissions and targets 2021 to 2025
facts: Updated 29 June 2026 with 2021 to 2025 HSE emissions and targets data.
The report includes annual targets and actual emissions for registered installations.
Installation-level actual emissions still require verified geometry before any parcel attribution.

sources.title: UK ETS Hospital and Small Emitter status
facts: The guidance describes HSE eligibility and 2026 to 2030 status.
Small emitters meet scheme thresholds including annual emissions and thermal input criteria.
Eligibility or target status is not a zero-emissions observation.

sources.title: UK ETS guidance for ultra-small emitters
facts: The 2026 to 2030 USE list covers qualifying installations below the scheme threshold.
USE installations must continue monitoring and notify the regulator if emissions exceed the threshold.
A threshold or opt-out status must not be interpreted as measured zero emissions.

sources.title: UK ETS installations: how to comply
facts: Updated 9 February 2026 for METS, deficit notices and 2026 allocation-period changes.
The guidance covers greenhouse-gas permits, monitoring, reporting and verification.
A permit or reporting workflow is not a physical emissions measurement.

sources.title: UK ETS technical guidance and tools
facts: Updated through 26 June 2026.
The collection includes reporting templates, technical guidance and annual emissions factor resources.
Templates and default factors remain methodology tools rather than observations.

sources.title: UK ETS MRR technical guidance
facts: Last updated 5 May 2026.
Guidance covers biomass, data-flow controls, sampling and voluntary waste MRV.
Monitoring guidance does not itself supply a measured emissions value.

sources.title: UK ETS Activity Level Report template
facts: Updated 20 February 2026 after correction of a formula error.
Operators use the template to report activity levels to regulators.
Activity-level reporting must not be treated as direct greenhouse-gas measurement.

sources.title: UK ETS policy overview
facts: The 2026 policy overview describes current UK ETS development including SAF and CORSIA interactions.
Policy design and future scheme changes are distinct from observed emissions.
Consultation or policy status must be preserved as such.

sources.title: UK ETS treatment of SAF consultation
facts: Published 23 March 2026 and closed 15 June 2026.
The consultation sought views on future treatment of SAF in the UK ETS.
A closed consultation is not a final rule or emissions observation.

sources.title: UK ETS SAF consultation accessible webpage
facts: Published 23 March 2026.
The document discusses zero rating, lifecycle emissions values, fossil comparators and CORSIA eligible fuels.
Lifecycle savings and accounting treatment must not be confused with direct tailpipe or parcel measurements.

sources.title: Implementing CORSIA consultation
facts: The consultation proposed UK implementation of CORSIA offsetting requirements and interaction with UK ETS.
It concerns regulatory design for international aviation.
Proposal status and scheme scope are not observed emissions.

sources.title: CORSIA UK government response
facts: The response describes CORSIA MRV, eligible fuel treatment and scheme interactions.
Verification and fuel-claim rules are regulatory evidence, not parcel observations.
CORSIA and UK ETS scopes must not be double counted.

sources.title: UK methane action plan
facts: Published 29 October 2025.
The plan covers UK actions to reduce methane across agriculture, waste and fuel supply.
Policy commitments and targets are not measured emissions.

sources.title: UK methane action plan accessible webpage
facts: The plan discusses upstream oil-and-gas methane intensity, flaring and venting reduction and gas-network leakage actions.
Methane intensity is a ratio and is not an absolute site emission without compatible production/activity data.
Projected or policy reductions must remain distinct from measured outcomes.

sources.title: Production Screening Directions 2026
facts: Published 4 March 2026 and updated 29 April 2026.
The page lists OPRED production screening decisions under environmental assessment processes.
A screening direction or approval is not a greenhouse-gas measurement.

sources.title: Oil and gas environmental submissions and determinations
facts: Last updated 17 April 2026.
The page provides access to regulatory applications and determinations for offshore oil and gas.
Application and determination records do not themselves quantify GHG emissions.

sources.title: Oil and gas environmental alerts and incident reporting
facts: Last updated 18 March 2026.
The guidance covers environmental alerts and PON incident reporting for offshore operations.
An incident report is not necessarily a quantified methane or GHG mass measurement.

sources.title: PPC Applications and Decisions 2026
facts: Published 17 April 2026.
The collection contains 2026 PPC applications and decisions for large combustion installations offshore.
Permit status and pollutant-control requirements are not direct GHG measurements.

sources.title: Oil and gas EEMS database
facts: EEMS is the UK offshore oil and gas environmental database.
It records measured and calculated emissions and discharge data from offshore installations.
Facility records and calculated values still do not imply cadastral parcel binding.

sources.title: NSTA 2027 production, flaring and venting consents exercise
facts: Published for the 2027 Annual Consents Exercise beginning 29 June 2026.
NSTA reviews production, flaring and venting consents against regulatory and emissions-reduction commitments.
Consent limits and basin trends are not parcel-level measured emissions.

sources.title: NSTA emissions reduction
facts: NSTA describes its offshore flaring and venting regime and emissions-reduction obligations.
The framework targets unnecessary flaring and venting and supports net-zero obligations.
Regulatory targets and plans are not observations.

sources.title: Boiler methane emissions research
facts: Published 26 May 2026.
The project used laboratory testing to quantify methane and hydrogen-blend emissions from domestic boilers.
Laboratory appliance measurements must not be promoted to building or parcel emissions without field activity and boundary evidence.

sources.title: Onshore oil and gas emissions monitoring
facts: The guidance covers monitoring of non-combusted methane, fugitive emissions, flaring and ambient methane at onshore sites.
Monitoring strategy, baseline and leak-detection requirements must be distinguished from quantified annual GHG mass.
Site monitoring does not automatically establish cadastral parcel attribution.

sources.title: Onshore oil and gas flares
facts: The guidance requires flare design and operational information including gas flow and combustion monitoring where applicable.
Feed-gas flow, temperature and flame status are process variables rather than automatically annual GHG mass.
Flaring must be distinguished from venting and fugitive methane.

sources.title: Environment Agency Methane Action Plan 2024 to 2026
facts: The Environment Agency plan covers methane-reduction regulatory actions in England through 2026.
Plans, enforcement priorities and knowledge-sharing actions are not measured emissions.
Policy evidence must remain separate from observational evidence.

sources.title: UK ETS baseline data collection 2025
facts: The page describes the 1 April to 30 June 2025 baseline data collection ahead of later allocation periods.
Baseline and free-allocation data are regulatory activity inputs.
Historical baseline activity must not be treated as current measured parcel GHG emissions.
